bibl.title: Science collaboration networks in sociology and their general characteristics in Serbia

person.p: the tag layer; a sentence written by the tagger about the paper, always anchored to a quotation but not itself a quotation

span.label: existence
span.quote: Based on this insight, we can conclude that the scientific networks of coauthors’ works of sociologists in Serbia are not quite developed.

span.label: scientific coauthorship networks in sociology
span.quote: Science collaboration networks occupy an important place in the analysis of social networks.

span.label: observational-study
span.quote: We have analysed coauthors’ works according to the criterion of belonging to the same or different scientific/educational institution.

span.label: mechanisms
span.term: 1990s isolation and economic collapse produced minimal science funding and minimal international contact, which suppressed the coauthorship that funding and contact would otherwise generate
span.quote: Among all else, it produced minimal investment in science, as well as hard and minimal international cooperation.

span.label: mechanisms
span.term: projects framed around very general themes let each associate work on his own issue without leaving his own profession, so participation never turns into joint problem-solving and hence not into coauthorship
span.quote: Problems related to the project are mostly chosen based on such general notion which could enable the project work of the associates who could tackle various issues, without the obligation to step out of their own profession.

span.label: mechanisms
span.term: the absence of distinguished scientists who gather younger associates leaves no nuclei around which collaboration networks could form
span.quote: In Serbian Sociology there are no distinguished scientists who tend to gather younger associates

span.label: The paper states it cannot readily explain why Serbian sociologists do not co-author.
span.quote: The question why the Serbian sociologists do not cooperate during the writing of scientific works cannot be answered easily.

span.label: The paper notes that its comparison is between scientific communities of very different sizes, so the author/coauthor distributions are not directly comparable.
span.quote: Considering the fact that the issue is about comparing scientific communities of various sizes, the samples of such a distribution of authors’ and coauthors’ works are quite different.

span.label: The field measures a thing it rarely defines: the paper states that very few works define what science collaboration is.
span.quote: However, there are very few works which define what science collaboration is.

span.label: The term rests on social convention, and what one researcher counts as collaboration another counts as a loose grouping.
span.quote: Katz and Martin (1997) concluded that the term of “collaboration” is hard to define, because it is in great measure a thing of social conventions between scientists. That which by some would be considered as collaboration, others could define as loose grouping or collection of informal connections

span.label: Each study narrows the term to one aspect, so the operational definitions differ between the works being compared.
span.quote: Researchers of the scientific networks more commonly opt for just one of its aspects and therefore narrow their operational definitions of science collaboration networks

span.label: Citation counts aggregate acts that mean opposite things, including citing to display reading and deliberately not citing a rival.
span.quote: Cole (1970) speaks about “ceremonial citation” as a demonstration in literature knowing and “diplomatic non-citation” as purposeful non-citation of authors from rival group

span.label: science collaboration
span.quote: However, there are very few works which define what science collaboration is.

span.label: coauthored work
span.quote: The connection exists if there is at least one coauthored work between two scientists

span.label: citation
span.quote: citation envelops many aspects: bibliographic pairing, co-citation, direct citation, symbolic citation, negative, diplomatic and auto citation

span.label: auto citation
span.quote: Separate problem for citation analysis is emergence of auto citation, which is widely spread in scientific works

span.label: core knowledge
span.quote: Sociology, as Cole (1994b; also see Škorić, 2010) further explains, does not have core knowledge

span.label: science collaboration - AS AT LEAST ONE SHARED BYLINE: in network analysis the authors are the nodes and a link exists if there is at least one coauthored work, so the relation is binary and carries no degree, duration or division of labour
span.quote: In this kind of analysis, the actors (nods) are authors, and connections (links) between them are coauthored works. The connection exists if there is at least one coauthored work between two scientists

span.label: science collaboration - AS A SOCIAL CONVENTION with moving boundaries: what counts is settled between scientists rather than by a criterion, and the paper says the boundary is prone to change
span.quote: The process of determining the boundaries of collaboration is prone to change

span.label: citation - SEVERAL DIFFERENT ACTS UNDER ONE NAME: bibliographic pairing, co-citation, direct, symbolic, negative, diplomatic and auto citation, which a count cannot tell apart
span.quote: citation envelops many aspects: bibliographic pairing, co-citation, direct citation, symbolic citation, negative, diplomatic and auto citation

span.label: extends → Moody (2004), The Structure of a Social Science Collaboration Network
span.quote: Therefore, it does not come as a surprise that the cooperation of the Serbian sociologists at the beginning of the 21st century was three times smaller than the cooperation of the sociologists portrayed in Moody’s research.

span.label: science collaboration —operationalised-as→ coauthored work
span.quote: In this kind of analysis, the actors (nods) are authors, and connections (links) between them are coauthored works. The connection exists if there is at least one coauthored work between two scientists

span.label: auto citation —is-a→ citation
span.quote: citation envelops many aspects: bibliographic pairing, co-citation, direct citation, symbolic citation, negative, diplomatic and auto citation

span.label: proportion
span.quote: The proportion of author works in total number of published texts is 89.1%, whereas the proportion of coauthor works is merely 10.9%.

span.label: frequency distribution
span.quote: Table 1: Frequency of authors’ and coauthors’ works in magazines Sociološki pregled, Sociologija and Teme for the period 2000-2010

span.label: Across three Serbian sociology journals for 2000-2010, single-authored papers overwhelmingly dominate: 89.1% of published texts against only 10.9% coauthored.
span.quote: The proportion of author works in total number of published texts is 89.1%, whereas the proportion of coauthor works is merely 10.9%.

span.label: Among the coauthored papers, collaboration between colleagues in the same institution is twice as frequent as collaboration across institutions.
span.quote: The conclusion is that the participation of coauthors who are employed in the same institutions is twice as higher than the participation of the authors who cooperate with the colleagues from the other scientific institutions (see table 1).

span.label: The authors conclude from these frequencies that coauthorship networks among Serbian sociologists are underdeveloped.
span.quote: Based on this insight, we can conclude that the scientific networks of coauthors’ works of sociologists in Serbia are not quite developed.

span.label: Serbian sociologists at the start of the 21st century collaborated three times less than the sociologists in Moody's international data.
span.quote: Therefore, it does not come as a surprise that the cooperation of the Serbian sociologists at the beginning of the 21st century was three times smaller than the cooperation of the sociologists portrayed in Moody’s research.

span.label: Kronegger and colleagues, applying the same methodology as Moody, arrive at a different network structure for sociology, which the authors attribute to the size of the national scientific community and its dependence on ministry funding.
span.quote: Even though Kronegger and his associates used the same methodology as Moody did, we have seen that the results of their research point out different network structures which are realised by the sociologists.

span.label: Although sociology is taught at three Serbian universities, none of their study programmes contains a course on the theory or analysis of social networks.
span.quote: there is not one subject which is dedicated to the theory and analysis of social networks in their study programmes.

span.label: In all four Slovenian disciplines examined, scientists preferentially form new coauthorships with the coauthors of their coauthors, closing triangles - a signature of small-world clustering within network borders.
span.quote: In all four disciplines, scientists are inclined to form new coauthorship connections with coauthors of their coauthors, which is irrefutable confirmation of high grouping inside network borders and a clear indicator of small-world network structures.

span.label: basic research unit of science collaboration
span.term: basic research unit of science collaboration
span.quote: The basic research unit of science collaboration is direct collaboration between two or more researchers, but it can also go on between research groups from one section, between sections of the same institution, between sectors, geographic regions and countries.

span.label: core knowledge / research frontier
span.quote: The core knowledge consists of small group of theories and methods which are almost universally accepted as true and important from the relevant scientific circles, while the research frontier is consist of all newly produced knowledge, the largest parts of it being rejected as wrong.

span.label: coauthorship network (actors and links)
span.quote: In this kind of analysis, the actors (nods) are authors, and connections (links) between them are coauthored works.

span.label: ceremonial citation / diplomatic non-citation
span.quote: Cole (1970) speaks about “ceremonial citation” as a demonstration in literature knowing and “diplomatic non-citation” as purposeful non-citation of authors from rival group etc.

span.label: preferential attachment, small-world and structural cohesion models
span.term: preferential attachment, small-world and structural cohesion models
span.quote: In order to discover that, he suggests the process of testing of three models: the preferential attachment model (in which the structure is based on “visible” authors), small-world model (where the scientists are grouped in loosely connected clusters) and structural cohesion model (which suggests all-encompassing connection within the large part of the network).

span.label: coauthors' institutional affiliation (same vs. different institution)
span.term: coauthors' institutional affiliation (same vs. different institution)
span.quote: We have analysed coauthors’ works according to the criterion of belonging to the same or different scientific/educational institution.

span.label: proportion of coauthored versus single-authored papers
span.term: proportion of coauthored versus single-authored papers
span.quote: The proportion of author works in total number of published texts is 89.1%, whereas the proportion of coauthor works is merely 10.9%.

span.label: 89.1% — share of single-authored papers in the three Serbian sociology journals, 2000-2010
span.quote: The proportion of author works in total number of published texts is 89.1%, whereas the proportion of coauthor works is merely 10.9%.

span.label: 10.9% — share of coauthored papers in the same three journals over the same period
span.quote: The proportion of author works in total number of published texts is 89.1%, whereas the proportion of coauthor works is merely 10.9%.

span.label: 33.2% — share of coauthored works in Sociological Abstracts 1963-1999, the comparison figure taken from Moody
span.quote: As Moody (2004: 222) concludes: out of 100% of the works published in Sociological Abstract, in the period between 1963 and 1999, only 33.2% belong to the coauthors’ works.

span.label: 3.00 — average network distance between Slovenian sociologists reported by Kronegger et al., against 3.97 in physics, 4.36 in biotechnology and 3.91 in mathematics
span.quote: Average distance between sociologists in Slovenia was 3.00 (for Physics it was 3.97, Biotechnology it was 4.36 and Mathematics 3.91).
